summary: Stream fallback (HTTP/2 -> WebSocket) drops idempotency header causing function-call executed twice across SDKs
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports that when their TypeScript client streams a chat session with function calling enabled, the first attempt executes the external tool exactly once. On a transient network blip the SDK falls back from HTTP/2 streaming to the WebSocket transport; the retry attempt results in the external function being invoked a second time despite the client attaching an idempotency key.

Impact: Potential double side-effects for external tools (webhooks, billing calls). Affected customer (DataScribe Inc.) sees duplicated downstream records and is blocking their production rollout. Affects both TS and Go SDKs when the proxy/network causes protocol downgrade during streaming handshakes.

Environment: prod-us-east, customer on Dedicated tier, using SDK v2.7.1 (ts) and v1.9.0 (go) with function_calling enabled. Gateway v3.2.0.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a streaming chat session with function calling (Function: /record-event) and attach header "Idempotency-Key: ds-evt-<uuid>" on the initial request.
2) Force a short TCP interruption (corporate proxy simulating HTTP/2 shutdown) causing the SDK to fallback to WebSocket.
3) SDK reconnects and issues a retry; external tool /record-event receives a second POST within ~700ms.

Observed logs (customer):
- TS SDK (client): "[stream-fallback] transport downgraded: http2 -> ws; retrying request with retry-id d6f8"
- Gateway (prod): "WARN stream-handshake: missing header Idempotency-Key on fallback-handshake session=abc123"
- Customer tool: two POSTs 2026-03-09T20:07:12.123Z and 2026-03-09T20:07:12.936Z, identical payload and different request-ids.

Expected behavior: When a client retries due to a transport downgrade, idempotency information provided by the client (Idempotency-Key) should be preserved and honored by the platform so that tool/function invocations are deduplicated.

Notes: Customer confirms they set Idempotency-Key in both header and client body in a subsequent test and saw deduplication succeed. They prefer a server-side guard by default rather than requiring clients to duplicate the key in body.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:12 - Aisha Patel (Support): Initial triage and acknowledgement. Asked customer for SDK versions and a HAR/network snapshot.

2026-03-10 11:05 - DataScribe Support Engineer (customer): Provided tcpdump and confirmed corporate proxy performs HTTP/2 connection close on large upstream frames; TS SDK logs show fallback behavior.

2026-03-10 14:30 - Marcus Lee (SRE): Reproduced locally using proxy simulation; observed gateway log 'missing header Idempotency-Key on fallback-handshake'. Raised INT-824 to investigate gateway handshake path.

2026-03-11 09:20 - Dev (gateway team): Noted that header forwarding for the initial HTTP2 stream metadata is split from the websocket handshake code path, and a conversion mapping currently misses some custom headers by design for safety.
2026-03-11 12:45 - Support: Shared short-term workaround (include key in body) and asked customer to validate.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 - Repro steps executed in lab: using local proxy to force HTTP/2 RST then allow SDK to open WS. Confirmed Idempotency-Key absent on WS handshake path when header was set only in initial HTTP/2 metadata.

Hypothesis: The api-gateway's stream downgrade path creates a new connection context for WebSocket and does not copy non-standard headers unless they are whitelisted. Idempotency-Key is not whitelisted currently to avoid exposing internal headers.

Cross-sdk observation: Go SDK includes idempotency key in request body by default for function calls (older behavior) which explains why some Go customers didn't observe duplication. TS SDK placed the key in a header only (v2.7.1).
Risk assessment: Medium-high for Dedicated customers behind aggressive proxies. Potential for financial or side-effect duplication depending on customer tool implementations.
Workaround viability: Customer can add idempotency key into the function_call payload/body; gateway will persist body fields across fallback. This is sufficient short-term.

Proposed fixes: (a) Whitelist Idempotency-Key header in gateway fallback handshake mapping (gateway PR pending). (b) Server-side dedupe by storing recent function invocation signature keyed by (customer_id, idempotency_key) for 60s. (c) SDK patch for TS to also include key in body for streaming retry scenarios.
resolution_notes: Mitigation (customer-facing): Instructed DataScribe to include Idempotency-Key in both header and body as a short-term workaround. Provided example snippet for TS and Go.

Planned work: gateway team opened PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/gateway/pull/198 to whitelist Idempotency-Key during fallback handshake. SDK team opened https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-ts/pull/4123 to add body fallback for idempotency in v2.8.0.
Follow-ups: INT-824 created for gateway integration tests. Support to schedule a post-deploy verification with customer after gateway PR and SDK v2.8.0 release.
Customer acceptance: DataScribe agreed to the workaround and asked for timeline for gateway fix. ETA requested: 3 business days for PR review + 1 day for canary deployment.
